title: Lech Lecha: new names (Genesis 17)
hook: Abram becomes Abraham, Sarai becomes Sarah, and the covenant of circumcision begins

segments.voice: Yesterday, the covenant between the pieces: count the stars, and a torch in the dark. Your line was the promise is long. Today, the last day of Lech Lecha.

A person can collect a lot of names in one life. The one on the birth certificate. A childhood nickname. The name a grandmother used. A name taken later, at a wedding, at a conversion, or just in growing up. Names aren't only labels. They carry who someone was, and sometimes who they're becoming. Abram is ninety-nine years old. He's been Abram his whole life. And God tells him that name is too small now. And the name grows by a single letter.
screen: `A LOT OF NAMES IN ONE LIFE.` → `WHO YOU WERE, WHO YOU'RE BECOMING.` → `A NAME GROWS BY ONE LETTER.`

segments.voice: God appears to Abram and says: walk before me, and be whole-hearted. Then: "Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for the father of a multitude of nations have I made thee." The verse itself explains the new name: Abraham, av hamon goyim, father of a multitude of nations. The change is one Hebrew letter: a heh, added in the middle. Then Sarai. God says: don't call her Sarai any more; Sarah shall be her name. She'll be blessed, and have a son, and be a mother of nations and kings. The Talmud reads Sarai as my princess, and Sarah as princess: at first she was a princess only to her own people; now she's a princess for the whole world. The ending that meant mine is dropped. She stops belonging to one household and starts belonging to everyone. Her name also changes by one letter: the yod at the end becomes a heh. Some teachers notice that heh is also a letter in God's name, and read it as if God gave each of them a piece of it. The Talmud goes further: Bar Kappara says that whoever still calls Abraham Abram transgresses a commandment. The new name is meant to stick. The same chapter begins the covenant of circumcision, brit milah, for Abraham and his household, and for every Jewish boy on the eighth day. By custom, that's when a Jewish boy is named: a covenant and a name, given together. So that's Lech Lecha, finished. The road ran everywhere. Be a blessing. Not a thread. A long promise in the dark. And a name that grows.
screen: `ABRAM BECOMES ABRAHAM.` · `SARAI BECOMES SARAH.` · `A HEH FOR EACH OF THEM.` · `A COVENANT AND A NAME TOGETHER.` · then, large: `A NAME CAN GROW.`

segments.voice: Say your name silently, slowly, the way someone who loves you would say it, and notice what it carries: who named you, what it means, the people who've said it kindly. Then ask who you're growing into, and imagine a letter added to your name, a small piece of something larger. Say your name once more, with that in it.
Lech Lecha. The portion that begins with go to yourself and ends with new names: Abraham, and Sarah.
Your line: a name can grow. Abram to Abraham, by a single letter. See you in Vayera.

howItsDone: Jewish boys are named at their brit milah on the eighth day, and girls are often named in the synagogue at a Torah reading or at a naming ceremony; Jews are called to the Torah by their Hebrew names.

notes: Meaning of 'Abram' ('exalted father') is the usual gloss; confirm.

Berakhot 13a: 'at first a princess to her own people, in the end to all the world'; and 'whoever calls Abraham Abram transgresses'. The script softens 'transgresses' to 'misses the point'; confirm the softening is acceptable.
The heh from God's name: Genesis Rabbah (and Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:6 on the yod of Sarai given to Joshua). Confirm citation.
Circumcision is described briefly and neutrally; girls' naming customs appear only in howItsDone.
